title: Presenting your capstone design
idea: A design presentation is a short, ordered story: the problem and scope, the model, one request traced through it, proof it runs, and the trade-offs you chose.
points: Open with scope: three use cases in, recurring meetings out, stated in one breath.
Show the class diagram once, then trace `book` end to end through it.
Show captured output: a taken room is rejected with `ROOM_TAKEN`, not a crash.
Close with trade-offs and one change you can absorb, such as a new `ConflictPolicy`.

items.label: Scope
items.text: State the brief, the actors, and what you deliberately left out.

items.label: Model
items.text: Walk the class diagram: `Room`, `Booking`, `BookingService`, the two repositories, and why each exists.

items.label: One request
items.text: Trace `book` from the service through `ConflictPolicy` to `BookingRepository` and the listeners.

items.label: Proof
items.text: Run the checks: a booking, a clash, a bad slot, a stranger cancelling.

items.label: Trade-offs
items.text: Name each choice and its cost, like in-memory repositories behind an interface.

items.label: Questions
items.text: Invite change questions and answer each with the one class that would change.

pitfalls: Reading every class aloud; listeners lose the thread. Trace one request instead.
Claiming 'it handles clashes' without showing the output that proves it.

quiz.q: A reviewer asks how you would add a 15-minute buffer between meetings. What is the strongest answer?
options: Add an if-check for the buffer inside `BookingService.book`
Inject a new `ConflictPolicy`; the service stays unchanged
Store the buffer as a field on every `Booking`
Say buffers are out of scope and move on
quiz.why: The overlap rule sits behind `ConflictPolicy`; your `CleaningGap(0.25)` is that buffer. Pass it to the `BookingService` constructor; only that wiring line changes.

takeaway: Tell one story: scope, model, one traced request, proof, trade-offs.

starters: Can you play a reviewer and ask me change questions about my booking design?
How do I explain why I used an interface for the repositories?
What should I do when I cannot answer a question during the presentation?
